analysis:
Examined both CLI-reference excerpts, installation metadata, the installation patch and BASE source. The supplied CLI head lines 2123–2545 are outside its complete changed ranges; their diagnostic capture, cache, authorization, cluster ownership and resource-limit descriptions do not establish new behavior in this PR. Installation HEAD lines 219–256 add operator-initiated predecessor rollback, confirmation, request draining, pair-stop requirements and exact-version quarantine while leaving automatic updates enabled. BASE installation lines 211–234 already describe crash-triggered quarantine and watchdog recovery; rollback itself is therefore not evidence of a newly bypassed security boundary.
No concrete regression is supported by these documentation units. Material integration questions remain for UpdateRollback.swift, UpdateInstallLayout.swift and the watchdog rollback implementation: independently validate predecessor identity/signature at use time, update-lease and journal atomicity, stopped-service behavior during confirmation, cluster refusal and quarantine persistence across restart/watchdog/startup checks. Relate the manual path to T-043/T-013 and ensure restored code still requires current build qualification and serving authorization under T-053/T-054/T-052; a signed older artifact alone grants neither. Do not infer acceptance of a revoked build from the offline rollback command. Also examine any changed recovery-state format for compatibility with the restored predecessor. These implementations are not supplied here, so their controls cannot be confirmed or reported as missing. No change to encryption, token custody, cache scoping (T-041), fan-helper authority or billing is demonstrated in this batch.
